knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The plan has no containment next to an occupied corridor, so work stops and the zoning is referred.
Section 4.3 sets this standard for complex work.
The route is planned so contamination does not cross clean or occupied space.

practicalCriteria: On a training sketch, the learner marks the zone, the clean route and the waste route, and shows that they do not cross each other.
In a described scene without containment, the learner stops work and writes the referral.
passRule: Knowledge checks only: three of three correct is a reading pass. It is not practical competence. Practical sign-off: an assessor observes each practical criterion and records it as met or not met.
evidenceRequired: Knowledge-check result recorded by the assessor
Completed training worksheet or role-play record for the scenario, marked by a trainer
stopWorkCriteria: Work starts in a complex zone before containment is approved.
Contaminated material passes through occupied or clean areas.
